inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report (URD), consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments' add-back EUR 37.3m (HO.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:17075); no net-share-settlement tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 across history). Interest income of EUR 116.8m (Note 6.1) is NOT stripped because the group is net-DEBT (EUR 1,618m incl. leases), so the cash pile is not added to EV; it is netted inside the company's net financial interest.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:15Z (Euronext Paris regular session, last print before the weekend; Yahoo chart API, state None)
inputs.share_count_basis: 206,430,005 shares in issue less 464,490 treasury = 205,965,515 outstanding at 31/12/2025 (Note 8.1), plus ~0.40m dilutive free-share/unit plans (Note 8.2 diluted denominator 205,879k vs basic 205,476k) = 206.4m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so grant dilution is already charged; buybacks (EUR 45m FY2025, EUR 275m FY2024, EUR 491m FY2023) are the funding mechanism for the flat count and are value-neutral here.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-denominated flows discounted at a EUR-built WACC: 10y OAT ~3.3% / Bund ~2.7% (blended risk-free 3.1%), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.95 for a European defence prime => cost of equity ~7.9%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.0% (S&P A- / Moody's A2, 2025 bond issuance), after tax ~2.3%; capital structure ~11% debt at market (gross debt EUR 6.1bn vs market cap ~EUR 47bn) => WACC 7.4%, rounded to 7.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, programme-execution and tax risk are charged in the flows via the scenario weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: IFRS 16 lease debt EUR 1,332.8m is INSIDE net_debt (the company's own net cash (debt) definition, Note 6.2: cash + ST investments 4,511.1 less financial debt 4,796.7 less lease debt 1,332.8 = net debt 1,618.4). Lease principal (EUR 235.8m FY2025) is therefore NOT deducted from the flows; instead right-of-use renewal is charged through the capex line, which is net operating investment (746) PLUS new lease liabilities (205.1) = EUR 951m = 4.3% of revenue. D&A includes right-of-use depreciation (EUR 233m) and is added back; EBITDA is post-IFRS-16. PPA amortisation (EUR 380.3m, Note 4.2) is excluded from both D&A and EBITDA so that EBITDA - SBC - D&A = Adjusted EBIT (EUR 2,740m) and tax is levied on Adjusted EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged once, in the bridge: book NCI is only EUR 19.3m but the adjusted profit share is EUR 26-34m/yr (two partly-owned subsidiaries; Note 8.1f says not material), so EUR 300m (~10x the adjusted NCI share) is deducted in equity_bridge rather than thinning the flows. Flows are 100% consolidated.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: non-US cyclical/industrial operating company -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Thales is an operating defence/aerospace/cyber prime with EUR 53.3bn order book; not a bank, REIT, holdco or distressed name. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry). CURRENCY: statements and flows in EUR, quote in EUR; fx_rate 1.0. PRICE is a regular-session print, not after-hours. ANCHOR STALENESS: the latest filing in the folder is the FY2025 annual (balance sheet 31/12/2025); the H1 2026 interim (published July 2026) has not been extracted, so net debt, share count and pensions are ten months old. Known moves since: EUR 3.90 dividend (~EUR 800m) paid May 2026, the F126 frigate-termination exceptional charge (EUR 330-450m per the Analysis), continued strong order intake. Re-anchor net debt when H1 2026 is extracted. OWNER FCF FY0: reported FCF (CSV) 2,565.1 = OCF 3,321.8 - capex 756.7, after net interest and after tax but before lease principal; last_fcf = 2,565.1 - SBC 37.3 - 0 interest income = 2,527.8 (formula-consistent anchor, levered). The forward build is UNLEVERED from components, so year-1 owner FCF (~EUR 2.1-2.2bn) is not directly comparable: it adds back after-tax net interest (~EUR 90m) and charges lease renewal (~EUR 205m) via capex. Cross-check: company FOCF 2,577 FY2025 (128% of Adjusted Net Income 2,005, inflated by a EUR 724m working-capital inflow from customer advances); FY2026 guidance 100-110% conversion on ~EUR 2.15bn ANI => FOCF ~EUR 2.15-2.35bn levered pre-lease, i.e. ~EUR 2.05-2.25bn unlevered post-lease-renewal, which brackets the base year-1 build. TAX: cash_tax_rate is applied to Adjusted EBIT (incl. EUR 213m equity-affiliate income, mainly Naval Group, which is post-tax -- a small conservative over-charge, ~EUR 50m/yr, accepted rather than stripping the income and adding an affiliate stake to the bridge). FY2025 adjusted tax was EUR 561m = 24.1% of adjusted pre-tax ex-affiliates, including the French temporary surtax (overall 36.13% vs normative 25.83%); FY2026 guided +EUR 90-100m surtax again. Expressed on total Adjusted EBIT: FY2026 ~22%, normalising to ~19.5-20% from FY2027 (French CIR research tax credit is booked in EBIT, so the P&L-based rate, not cash tax paid net of credits (EUR 413m, EUR 185m), is the right rate to apply). WORKING CAPITAL: positive capture on revenue growth -- contract liabilities (customer advances) EUR 12.4bn grow with the defence backlog (+EUR 843m in FY2025); base 12% of the revenue increase is well below the FY2025 46% capture and consistent with the 95-105% medium-term conversion target. PENSIONS: net pension liability EUR 1,420m (Note 9.3) deducted after tax in the bridge; service cost is in Adjusted EBIT, deficit-reduction contributions are not in the flows (no double charge). HISTORICAL DISCONTINUITY: FY2020 onward is restated ex-Transport (sold to Hitachi Rail, closed May 2024, EUR 412m gain in FY2024 net income); CAGRs use FY2020/FY2022 bases, both ex-Transport. FY2024 EPS 6.89 includes EUR 2.00 of discontinued gain; FY2025 8.13 is continuing-only.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company definition at 31/12/2025 (Note 6.2): cash and equivalents 4,446.5 + other current financial assets 64.6 = 4,511.1; financial debt 4,796.7 (LT 3,999.4 + ST 2,130.1 incl. lease) + lease debt 1,332.8 = gross debt 6,129.5; net debt 1,618.4. Pensions, NCI and the F126 charge are handled in equity_bridge, not in net_debt.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance (organic +6-7%, EUR 23.3-23.6bn) and the 2024-2028 CMD target of 5-7% organic CAGR at the upper end; cross-checked against the 7.6-8.0% revenue CAGRs (which include Imperva/Cobham M&A and a Covid-depressed FY2020 base)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (3.6%) diverges >30% from revenue (8.0%) and EPS (15.5%) CAGRs: equity is held down by a 40% dividend payout, EUR 1.1bn of buybacks 2022-24 and a EUR -726m cumulative translation adjustment (USD weakness), not by weak earnings. Equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2020 762.6, FY2021 2,230.9, FY2022 2,468.0, FY2023 861.4, FY2024 2,063.3, FY2025 2,527.8. The series is dominated by working-capital timing on customer advances (FY2022 +, FY2023 -, FY2025 +724) so FCF CAGRs (0.8% 3yr, 27.1% 5yr) carry no signal; SBC is immaterial (0.1-0.3% of revenue) and is not growing faster than cash flow. All windows are ex-Transport (FY2020 restated), so the FY2019->FY2020 Transport deconsolidation does not enter any CAGR. EPS CAGRs are flattered by the FY2020 Covid trough (2.27) and the FY2024 figure includes a EUR 2.00/share discontinued gain.

base.ebit_margin_note: Implied Adjusted EBIT margin (EBITDA - SBC - D&A): 12.7, 13.1, 13.5, 13.7, 13.8, 13.9, 14.0 then flat -- FY2026 at the guided 12.6-12.8% midpoint, FY2028 at the CMD 13-14% midpoint, maturing at 14.0% (the CMD top end) by FY2032.
base.growth_note: FY2026 +6.0% reported (guidance +6-7% organic less ~1pt USD translation drag at EUR/USD 1.18); FY2027-28 +6% (upper half of the 5-7% CMD range); decelerating to 2.5% by year 10 as the European rearmament ramp plateaus.
base.capex_note: Includes ROU lease additions (~0.9% of revenue). FY2026-27 at 4.6% reflects the guided step-up from EUR 746m net operating investment for capacity; fades to 4.0% vs 3.4% D&A at maturity.
base.wc_note: 12% of the YoY revenue increase: customer advances on a growing defence backlog; the FY2025 capture was 46% and management guides 100-110% FOCF conversion for FY2026.

bull.ebit_margin_note: Implied Adjusted EBIT margin: 12.8, 13.4, 14.0, 14.4, 14.7, 15.0 flat -- above the CMD 13-14% range by FY2029 on defence operating leverage, Space turning EBIT-positive and Avionics/IFE recovery.

bear.ebit_margin_note: Implied Adjusted EBIT margin: 12.4, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5 flat -- the FY2026 guidance is missed at the low end and the 2028 13-14% target is not reached; French surtax becomes permanent (21% on EBIT); no working-capital tailwind as book-to-bill drops to ~1.

scenario_narratives.base: Thales delivers the FY2026 guidance (organic +6-7%, Adjusted EBIT margin 12.6-12.8%, book-to-bill >1.1, cash conversion 100-110%) and the 2024-2028 CMD roadmap at the upper half: ~6% organic growth through FY2028 on the EUR 53bn order book (Defence EUR 41.6bn = 3.4 years of segment sales) and European rearmament, Adjusted EBIT margin reaching 13.5% in FY2028 and maturing at 14.0% by FY2032 as defence operating leverage and the Avionics/IFE recovery outweigh a sluggish Cyber & Digital (payment cards, connectivity) and the Space restructuring. Capex steps up for capacity in FY2026-27 and fades; the French surtax rolls off after FY2026; customer advances keep working capital a modest tailwind (12% of revenue growth). Growth decelerates to 2.5% terminal as budgets plateau in the 2030s.
scenario_narratives.bull: The rearmament cycle lasts 'about a generation' as management frames it: NATO 3.5% GDP core targets lift Defence growth to 8% in FY2027-28 (book-to-bill stays >1.2), Space turns EBIT-positive inside the Airbus-Leonardo-Thales combination, Avionics rides the Airbus/Boeing production ramp, Cyber & Digital returns to growth post-Imperva integration, and group Adjusted EBIT margin passes the CMD range to 15% by FY2031. Customer advances capture 15% of revenue growth, the normalised tax rate settles at 19%, terminal growth 3% with a 20x FCF cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Defence order momentum fades (a Ukraine settlement or European budget consolidation pulls book-to-bill to ~1), programme execution bites again after F126 (fixed-price overruns, offset obligations in India/UAE), Space losses persist if the three-way combination stalls, and Cyber & Digital keeps shrinking on physical-card declines and Broadcom/Cloudflare competition. Growth slows to 2% by FY2031, the Adjusted EBIT margin stalls at ~12.5% (FY2026 guidance missed, 2028 target abandoned), the French surtax becomes structural (21% on EBIT), no working-capital tailwind, terminal growth 2% with a 16x cap. The group remains solidly profitable and A-rated throughout: this is a stalled-re-rating case, not a solvency case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20%: the F126 cancellation shows programme-execution risk is live on fixed-price naval/defence work, the French surtax has already been renewed once and may become permanent, and Cyber & Digital (17% of sales) is in decline. Bull trimmed from 35% to 30% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (defence budgets sustained at 3.5% GDP, Space turnaround via a still-unapproved three-way merger, and Cyber & Digital growth) on top of the already-guided defence ramp. No going-concern or covenant risk (A-/A2, EUR 1.5bn undrawn line, net debt 0.5x EBITDA), so bear stays well below 30%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Thales is valued as an operating cash-flow compounder on an unlevered owner-FCF basis built from components anchored to the FY2025 adjusted income statement and the FY2026 guidance, with IFRS 16 leases treated as debt, pensions and NCI deducted in the bridge, the terminal value capped at 18x FCF (Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% would be 20.5x), and SBC -- immaterial at 0.17% of revenue -- expensed with a flat share count. The house and street bases are nearly coincident because SBC is tiny; band_position is close to degenerate and should be read as such. Value is dominated by the terminal (roughly 60% of EV), so the WACC x terminal-growth grid and the 18x cap matter more than any single year's driver.
key_risks_to_valuation: Balance-sheet anchors are from 31/12/2025; the H1 2026 interim (F126 provision, May 2026 dividend, H1 cash flow) is not yet extracted -- net debt could be EUR 0.5-1.0bn different
Defence cycle duration: 60% of sales to governments; a peace settlement or budget consolidation would cut the growth path and the working-capital tailwind together
Programme execution on fixed-price contracts (F126 precedent) -- a single large overrun is EUR 0.3-0.5bn, ~EUR 1.5-2.5/share each time
French fiscal policy: the temporary surtax (EUR 90-100m/yr) is modelled as rolling off after FY2026 in base; permanence is worth ~EUR 4-5/share

Working-capital capture: FY2025 FOCF was 128% of ANI on a EUR 724m advance inflow; the model assumes 12% capture of revenue growth, and an unwind of advances in a flat-order year would push a year's FCF well below the build
Space (Thales Alenia Space) restructuring and the Airbus-Leonardo-Thales combination (2027 target) -- deconsolidation could change the perimeter materially
Terminal value: ~60% of EV; the 18x cap binds in base, so the valuation is effectively 18x year-10 FCF plus ten years of flows
Equity-affiliate income (EUR 213m, mainly Naval Group 35%) is inside Adjusted EBIT and taxed again in the build; cash dividends from affiliates are lower than the equity-accounted share
